examples.solution_text:
Add the numerators and keep the common denominator.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{6}{a}+\frac{7}{a}\\&=\frac{6+7}{a}\\&=\frac{13}{a}\end{aligned}$

The lowest common denominator is $x^2$. Multiply the first numerator and denominator by $x$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{8}{x}-\frac{3}{x^2}\\&=\frac{8x}{x^2}-\frac{3}{x^2}\\&=\frac{8x-3}{x^2}\end{aligned}$

The lowest common denominator is $ab$. Multiply the second numerator and denominator by $a$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{7}{ab}+\frac{2}{b}\\&=\frac{7}{ab}+\frac{2a}{ab}\\&=\frac{7+2a}{ab}\end{aligned}$

Multiply the numerators and denominators, then divide by common factors.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{8a}{7b}\times\frac{14b^2}{12a^3}\\&=\frac{112ab^2}{84a^3b}\\&=\frac{112b}{84a^2}\\&=\frac{4b}{3a^2}\end{aligned}$

Multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{3m}{8}\div\frac{9m}{20}\\&=\frac{3m}{8}\times\frac{20}{9m}\\&=\frac{60m}{72m}\\&=\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}$

Write $4$ over $1$ and multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4\div\frac{3}{5x}\\&=\frac{4}{1}\times\frac{5x}{3}\\&=\frac{20x}{3}\end{aligned}$

Multiply by the reciprocal, then cancel common factors using the index law for division.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{5x^2}{6y^4}\div\frac{10x^5}{3y}\\&=\frac{5x^2}{6y^4}\times\frac{3y}{10x^5}\\&=\frac{15x^2y}{60x^5y^4}\\&=\frac{15}{60x^3y^3}\\&=\frac{1}{4x^3y^3}\end{aligned}$

Simplify the product inside the brackets first.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{5p^2}{6q}\times\frac{2}{p}\\&=\frac{10p^2}{6pq}\\&=\frac{5p}{3q}\end{aligned}$
Then multiply by its reciprocal.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{10p}{3q}\div\frac{5p}{3q}\\&=\frac{10p}{3q}\times\frac{3q}{5p}\\&=\frac{30pq}{15pq}\\&=2\end{aligned}$
